one_liner: Header-only C/C++ single-precision approximations of exp, log, pow, sigmoid, trig, erf, lgamma and Lambert W, with SSE2 variants; no measured speedup over libm.
what_it_does: Paul Mineiro's library of approximate float versions of common libm functions, each in a 'fast' (about 1e-4 average error on the tests' metric) and a 'faster' (about 2e-2) tier, plus four-wide SSE2 v4sf versions (vfastexp, vfastlog, ...). They are free static inline functions with libm-like scalar signatures (fastexp(float), fastpow(float, float)), so swapping a call is a rename, but the results are approximate and the input domain is narrower than libm's. Ship either the split headers under fastapprox/src or the single fastonebigheader.h.
how_it_is_fast: It works on the IEEE-754 bit pattern instead of doing range reduction and polynomials: the 'faster' variants are Schraudolph-style tricks (exp2 builds the float bits as 2^23 * (p + 126.94), log2 reads the raw bits as an integer and rescales), and the 'fast' variants add a small rational correction on the mantissa fraction (for example 27.728 / (4.8425 - z) in pow2). Sigmoid, pow, sinh, cosh and tanh are composed from these; sin and cos use a parabola-plus-correction approximation on [-pi, pi]; there are no branches except input clamps, so the SSE2 versions are straight-line code.
when_to_use: Machine-learning or probabilistic inner loops (logistic loss, softmax-like weights, digamma and lgamma in variational updates) that tolerate about 1e-4 relative error and keep arguments in moderate ranges.
SSE2 batch evaluation of exp, log or sigmoid where a full vector math library is too heavy to pull in.
Plain C codebases that want a single BSD-licensed header with no dependencies.
Graphics, audio or game code that only needs 2-3 correct digits and can use the 'faster' tier.
As a reference for the bit-manipulation techniques (the repo includes a Mathematica notebook explaining them).
when_not_to_use: Inputs outside the tested ranges: fastexp/fasterexp return NaN or a negative number instead of +inf for x above about 88.7, so fastsigmoid(x) returns NaN, 1.0 or a small negative number instead of nearly 0 for x below about -88.7, and fasttanh(x) returns NaN or +1 instead of -1 just below x = -44.4 (fasttanh(-45) and fasttanh(-50) give +1).
Code that relies on libm special values: fastlog(0) is about -88.0 instead of -inf, fastlog(-1) about +177 instead of NaN, and NaN or inf inputs give finite values near 89.

When you need a documented speedup: the repo never times libm, and the author's own fasttrig.h comment says fastsinfull, fastcosfull and fasttanfull can be slower than libc on older machines and only slightly faster on newer ones.
Double precision, faithfully rounded results or reproducible ulp bounds: everything is float and accuracy is only checked as an average.
AVX2, AVX-512 or NEON vectorization: only SSE2 four-wide variants exist, and the project has had no commits since 2017.

integration.min_toolchain: C99 or C++ (GCC or Clang vector extensions for the C SSE2 path; MSVC supported for C++ through operator overloads added in the 2017 patch)
integration.platforms: any for the scalar functions; x86 with SSE2 for the v4sf variants, which are compiled only when __SSE2__ is defined (MSVC does not define that macro by default, so the vector variants are absent there unless it is defined by hand)
integration.thread_safety: reentrant pure functions (no global mutable state, only static const constants), from reading the source; not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same scalar float signatures as expf/logf/powf/sinf/tanhf under different names, but approximate (about 1e-4 or 2e-2 average error) and without libm's handling of overflow, zero, negative, NaN and infinite inputs

gotchas: Overflow bug outside the tested domain (checked this session by compiling a transcription of fastexp.h formulas with GCC -O2 on x86-64): fastexp(89) and fasterexp(89) return NaN, fastexp(90) returns -9.3e-39 and fastexp(200) returns -6.2e9 where expf returns inf, because the 2^23 * (p + 121.27 + ...) bit pattern spills past the exponent field into the sign bit and nothing clamps the top end; vfasterexp returns -0.0 there. The composed functions inherit it: fastsigmoid(-90) and fastersigmoid(-90) return 1.0 (true value about 8e-40) and fasttanh(-45) returns +1.0 instead of -1.0. The tests never see this because they sample exp on [-5, 5], sigmoid on [-50, 50] and sinh and cosh on [-25, 25]; inputs past the 2^32 limit make the float-to-uint32 cast undefined behaviour. Clamp arguments yourself.

The tests' accuracy metric is |est - exact| / (1e-4 + |est| + |exact|) and only its average over 100000 samples is asserted (max error is printed, not checked): it is about half the usual relative error and becomes an absolute-error test for outputs below 1e-4, so the '1e-4' figure understates the conventional relative error, especially for small sigmoid outputs.
The timing macro in tests/testmacros.h runs the approximation 1e8 times on a volatile constant 1.0f with gettimeofday and never runs libm, so the printed million calls per second is not a comparison.

Type punning goes through unions, which is defined in C but formally undefined in C++ (GCC, Clang and MSVC accept it); cast.h's include guard never defines __CAST_H_, which is harmless because the macro is redefined identically.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick fastapprox over SLEEF when 1e-4 average error is acceptable and you want one dependency-free header with sigmoid, lgamma, digamma, erf-inverse and Lambert W in it; pick SLEEF (1-ulp, AVX2/AVX-512/NEON, maintained) or fast_math_cpp (scalar float approximations with measured speed against glibc) when you need stated accuracy bounds or a measured speedup.
verified_claims_summary: No speed comparison against libm exists: the repo's tests assert that average error on the metric above stays under 1e-4 (fast tier) and 2e-2 (faster tier) against expf, logf, powf, sigmoid built from expf, sinf and others over 100000 drand48 samples in fixed ranges, and time only the approximation on a constant input with no compiler, flags or CPU recorded. The only first-party speed statement is directional and partly negative (fasttrig.h: the full-range trig versions can be slower than libc on older machines).
status_note: Abandoned since the 2017-03-01 MSVC and gcc narrowing merge (ChangeLog stops at 0.3.2), BSD-3-Clause per fastapprox/COPYING and small enough to vendor, but the unclamped exp overflow that breaks sigmoid and tanh for large negative arguments must be patched or guarded by the caller.
